lines.text: There are more possible chess games than atoms in the universe.
And it explodes after just four moves.
White starts with twenty possible first moves.
lines.caption: White starts with 20 possible first moves.

lines.text: After both players move once, there are four hundred possible games.
lines.caption: After both players move once, there are 400 possible games.

lines.text: After two moves each? Almost two hundred thousand.
lines.caption: After two moves each? Almost 200,000.

lines.text: Mathematician Claude Shannon estimated there are at least ten to the hundred and twentieth possible games.
lines.caption: Mathematician Claude Shannon estimated there are at least 10^120 possible games.

lines.text: The observable universe has only about ten to the eightieth atoms.
lines.caption: The observable universe has only about 10^80 atoms.
